lede: Spend so far this month, the average of the last three payments, the largest transfer to date: each is an aggregate over a slice of rows that moves with the current row. A window **frame** says which slice, so `sum`, `avg` and `max` can run along the rows instead of collapsing them.
objectives: Compute running totals, counts and maximums with an aggregate `.over(w)`
Choose a frame with `rowsBetween`, from the first row to the current one or a fixed number of rows back
Explain why the default frame adds tied rows together, and avoid it with a tie-breaker
Put a whole-group total on every row with a window that has no `orderBy`

blocks.md:
`transactions` has one row per movement on a bank account: `account_id`, when it was `posted_at`, its `direction` (`debit` when money leaves, `credit` when it arrives), a positive `amount` and a `status`. It's loaded as a DataFrame, and `F` is `pyspark.sql.functions`.

The examples look at **spending**: posted debits. Any aggregate you know from `groupBy` can also run over a window: `F.sum("amount").over(w)`. Instead of one total per group, every row gets the total of its **frame**, the rows of its window that the frame picks out.

For a running total, the frame runs from the first row of the partition to the current row: `rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)`.

blocks.title: Running spend per account
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spend = transactions.filter((F.col("direction") == "debit") & (F.col("status") == "posted"))

w = (Window.partitionBy("account_id").orderBy("posted_at", "transaction_id")
     .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow))

spend.select(
    "account_id", "posted_at", "amount",
    F.sum("amount").over(w).alias("spend_so_far"),
    F.count("*").over(w).alias("payments_so_far"),
    F.max("amount").over(w).alias("largest_so_far"),
).orderBy("account_id", "posted_at").show()
blocks.note: A00001's spend grows 27.90, 43.89, 63.12 as each payment is added. One transaction lost its account, so it forms a group of its own with a NULL `account_id`.

blocks.md:
The frame counts rows relative to the current one. `rowsBetween(-2, Window.currentRow)` is the current row and the two before it: a **moving** window of up to three rows. At the start of a partition there are fewer rows to take, so the first frames are shorter.

`Window.currentRow` is 0, so `rowsBetween(-2, 0)` means the same.

blocks.title: The last three transactions
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

posted = transactions.filter((F.col("status") == "posted") & (F.col("account_id") == "A00001"))

last3 = Window.partitionBy("account_id").orderBy("posted_at", "transaction_id").rowsBetween(-2, 0)

posted.select(
    "posted_at", "direction", "amount",
    F.sum("amount").over(last3).alias("last3_total"),
    F.avg("amount").over(last3).alias("last3_avg"),
    F.count("*").over(last3).alias("rows_in_frame"),
).orderBy("posted_at").show()
blocks.note: The first row averages one amount, the second two, and from the third on always three. `rows_in_frame` shows it. The average of decimals is a decimal with extra places.

blocks.md:
What if you give the window an `orderBy` and no frame? Spark then uses a default frame: from the first row up to the current row **and every row tied with it** on the order columns. For a running total that's a trap: two rows with the same timestamp get the same total, both including each other.

The fix is the same as for `row_number`: order by enough columns that no two rows tie, or say `rowsBetween` explicitly. Doing both is safest.

blocks.title: Ties and the default frame
blocks.code:
from decimal import Decimal
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

pays = spark.createDataFrame(
    [("P1", "A1", 1, Decimal("10.00")), ("P2", "A1", 2, Decimal("5.00")), ("P3", "A1", 2, Decimal("7.00")), ("P4", "A1", 3, Decimal("1.00"))],
    "pay_id STRING, account_id STRING, day INT, amount DECIMAL(12,2)",
)

default_frame = Window.partitionBy("account_id").orderBy("day")
by_rows = Window.partitionBy("account_id").orderBy("day", "pay_id").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

pays.select(
    "pay_id", "day", "amount",
    F.sum("amount").over(default_frame).alias("default_frame"),
    F.sum("amount").over(by_rows).alias("rows_frame"),
).orderBy("day", "pay_id").show()
blocks.note: P2 and P3 share day 2, so the default frame gives both 22.00: everything up to and including day 2. With a tie-breaker and `rowsBetween`, the total grows one row at a time: 15.00, then 22.00.

blocks.md: Leave out `orderBy` and the frame is the whole partition, so every row gets the group's total. That puts a group figure next to each row without a `groupBy`: here, each payment next to the account's total spend and what was still to come.

blocks.title: The whole group's total on every row
blocks.code:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

spend = transactions.filter((F.col("direction") == "debit") & (F.col("status") == "posted") & (F.col("account_id") == "A00001"))

whole = Window.partitionBy("account_id")
so_far = Window.partitionBy("account_id").orderBy("posted_at", "transaction_id").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

spend.select(
    "posted_at", "amount",
    F.sum("amount").over(whole).alias("account_total"),
    (F.sum("amount").over(whole) - F.sum("amount").over(so_far)).alias("still_to_come"),
).orderBy("posted_at").show()
blocks.note: Every row shows the same total, 63.12. Subtracting the running total leaves the spend after each payment, 0.00 on the last.

concept.prompt: Amounts in order are 10, 20, 30, 40. What does `F.sum("amount")` over `rowsBetween(-1, 0)` give on the row with 30?
concept.why: The frame is the previous row and the current one: 20 + 30 = 50.

concept.prompt: A window has `orderBy("posted_at")` and no frame. Two payments share a timestamp. What happens to a running sum on those rows?
choices: Both rows get the same total, which includes both payments
Each row adds only its own payment
concept.why: The default frame runs to the current row and every row tied with it. Add a tie-breaker and `rowsBetween` to grow one row at a time.

choices: The account's total on every one of its rows
An error, because the window has no order
concept.why: Without `orderBy`, the frame is the whole partition. Unlike ranking functions, aggregates don't need an order.

review: Any aggregate can run over a window: `F.sum("amount").over(w)` keeps every row.
`rowsBetween(-2, 0)` is a moving frame of the current row and the two before it; early frames are shorter.
With `orderBy` and no frame, tied rows are added together. Break ties and say `rowsBetween`.
Without `orderBy`, the frame is the whole partition: every row gets the group total.
Order windows fully so running figures don't change between runs.
